hints: Look at the carbonate decomposition temperatures first, since thermal stability tells you where X sits relative to calcium in Group 2.
X decomposes at 1150 C compared to 840 C for calcium, so X is below calcium with a larger cation, and sulfates get less soluble down the group.
Remember hydroxides show the opposite trend to sulfates down Group 2, so combine a much smaller sulfate value with a larger hydroxide value than calcium to pick the pair.
walkthrough:
**Place X in Group 2 from carbonate stability**

Think of carbonate decomposition as the carbonate ion being polarised by the metal cation. A smaller, more highly polarising cation distorts it more, so it decomposes more easily at a lower temperature.

Stability increases down Group 2: $$\text{MgCO}_3 < \text{CaCO}_3 < \text{SrCO}_3 < \text{BaCO}_3$$
Since X carbonate needs 1150 $^{\circ}$C versus only 840 $^{\circ}$C for $\text{CaCO}_3$, X must be below calcium, so $\text{X}^{2+}$ is larger than $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.

**Apply the sulfate solubility trend**

Solubility of Group 2 sulfates decreases down the group. As the cation gets larger, the lattice energy falls less quickly than the hydration energy, so dissolving becomes less favourable.

Trend: $$\text{MgSO}_4 \text{ (very soluble)} > \text{CaSO}_4 > \text{SrSO}_4 > \text{BaSO}_4 \text{ (very insoluble)}$$
Therefore $\text{XSO}_4$ must be less soluble than $4.66 \times 10^{-3}$ mol per 100 g water. That leaves only $7.11 \times 10^{-5}$.

**Apply the hydroxide solubility trend**

Hydroxides do the opposite, they get more soluble down the group. Here the small hydroxide anion means lattice energy falls faster than hydration energy as the cation grows.

Trend: $$\text{Mg(OH)}_2 \text{ (insoluble)} < \text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2 \text{ (soluble)}$$
Therefore $\text{X(OH)}_2$ must be more soluble than $1.53 \times 10^{-3}$ mol per 100 g water. That leaves only $3.37 \times 10^{-3}$.

**Combine both trends**

X is below calcium, so low sulfate solubility plus high hydroxide solubility. That combination is $7.11 \times 10^{-5}$ for the sulfate and $3.37 \times 10^{-3}$ for the hydroxide.

options.A: Sulfate value is correct because it is lower than calcium, showing decreased solubility down the group. Hydroxide value is wrong because $2.00 \times 10^{-5}$ is lower than calcium, but hydroxides become more soluble down the group, not less.
options.B: This is correct. X is below calcium from its higher carbonate decomposition temperature. Sulfate solubility decreases down Group 2, so $7.11 \times 10^{-5} < 4.66 \times 10^{-3}$ fits. Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2, so $3.37 \times 10^{-3} > 1.53 \times 10^{-3}$ fits.
options.C: Both values are the wrong way round. $1.83 \times 10^{-1}$ suggests sulfate solubility increases down the group, and $2.00 \times 10^{-5}$ suggests hydroxide solubility decreases. This swaps the two Group 2 trends.
options.D: Hydroxide value is correct because it is higher than calcium, showing increased solubility down the group. Sulfate value is wrong because $1.83 \times 10^{-1}$ is much higher than calcium, but sulfates become less soluble down the group.
